an8.5:1.1: “Bhikkhus, these eight worldly conditions revolve around the world, and the world revolves around these eight worldly conditions.
an8.5:1.3: Gain and loss, disrepute and fame, blame and praise, and pleasure and pain.
an8.5:1.4: These eight worldly conditions revolve around the world, and the world revolves around these eight worldly conditions.”
an8.5:2.1: Gain and loss, disrepute and fame,
an8.5:2.2: blame and praise, pleasure and pain:
an8.5:2.4: are impermanent, transient, and subject to change.
an8.5:3.1: A wise and mindful person knows them
an8.5:3.2: and sees that they are subject to change.
an8.5:3.3: Desirable conditions don’t excite his mind
an8.5:3.4: nor is he repelled by undesirable conditions.
an8.5:4.1: He has dispelled attraction and repulsion;
an8.5:4.2: they are gone and no longer present.
an8.5:4.3: Having known the dustless, sorrowless state,
an8.5:4.4: he understands rightly and has transcended existence.
